learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes, and a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: net particle movement
items.prompt: Dye molecules spread through still water from a region of high dye concentration toward regions of lower dye concentration. Which concept best describes the net change?
options: Active transport against a concentration gradient
Osmosis of water through a selective membrane
Dynamic equilibrium with no net concentration change
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: follow the moving species
items.prompt: Two solutions are separated by a membrane that water can cross but sucrose cannot. Side L has more sucrose than side R. Which statement identifies the expected process?
options: Sucrose actively moves from L to R through the membrane
Sucrose diffuses from R to L until its amount doubles
Water moves from R to L by osmosis
Water moves from L to R by active transport
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: identify the energy condition
items.prompt: A membrane protein uses energy released from ATP to move calcium ions from lower calcium concentration to higher calcium concentration. Which concept fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: distinguish motion from net change
items.prompt: At equilibrium, oxygen molecules cross a membrane in both directions at equal average rates. Which description is most accurate?
options: Oxygen is being pumped in both directions using ATP
Only water can cross the membrane
Equal opposing diffusion gives zero net movement
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: classify a membrane process
items.prompt: A cell is placed in a solution with a lower solute concentration than its cytoplasm. The membrane permits water but not the solute to cross. What process most directly causes the cell to gain water?
options: Active transport of water using ATP
Osmosis across the selectively permeable membrane
Diffusion of trapped solute out of the cell
Dynamic equilibrium before any water moves
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: relate equilibrium to diffusion
items.prompt: A particle diagram shows equal concentrations on both sides of a permeable membrane. Arrows of equal size point left and right, and particles remain in constant motion. Which relationship is represented?
options: Osmosis has stopped because every particle is stationary
Active transport maintains unequal concentrations without energy
Two-way diffusion persists at dynamic equilibrium
Solute crosses only from right to left until concentrations become unequal
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: apply the concept feature frame
items.prompt: Which feature is required for osmosis but not for a general case of solute diffusion?
options: Net water movement across a selectively permeable barrier
Movement from lower toward higher concentration using energy
Equal concentrations at the beginning of the process
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify a new selective barrier
items.prompt: A membrane allows water to cross but blocks dissolved protein. Compartment A has more dissolved protein than compartment B. Which immediate net movement is expected?
options: Protein moves from A to B by simple diffusion
Protein moves from B to A by active transport
Water moves from A to B by osmosis
Water moves from B to A by osmosis
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: separate movement from net flux
items.prompt: Which observation is sufficient to identify dynamic equilibrium for a diffusible solute?
options: Particles are visible on only one side of a barrier
Opposing particle fluxes are equal while particles still move
A pump consumes ATP as it moves the solute
Water crosses while the solute remains trapped
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: interpret balanced arrows
items.prompt: A table reports 24 molecules crossing left-to-right and 24 crossing right-to-left during the same interval. Concentrations stay equal. What does the table show?
options: Active transport creates a larger left-side concentration
All molecular motion has stopped during the interval
Dynamic equilibrium with ongoing diffusion and zero net transfer
Osmosis moves trapped solute across a selective membrane
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: closed-system total
items.prompt: A sealed flask has a total mass of 42.6 g before a reaction and 42.6 g after the reaction. Which principle is directly instantiated?
options: Output is inversely proportional to input
Mass is conserved in the closed system
A hidden catalyst must have been consumed
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: look for the opposing response
items.prompt: Body temperature rises above a reference value. Sweating increases, and temperature then moves back toward the reference value. Which principle is most directly represented?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: compare a ratio
items.prompt: A sensor produces 2 mV at 1 unit, 6 mV at 3 units, and 10 mV at 5 units. Which relationship is supported over the measured range?
options: The output is constant as input changes
The output is inversely proportional to input
The output shows negative feedback toward 2 mV
The output is directly proportional to input
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: keep the conclusion bounded
items.prompt: In a closed circuit, 0.40 A enters a junction through one branch. Currents of 0.15 A and 0.25 A leave through two branches. Which principle is instantiated?
options: The junction creates 0.40 A of new current
Current is conserved at the junction
Resistance must be zero in every branch
Voltage is directly proportional to time
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: identify the principle from a perturbation
items.prompt: A regulated concentration is briefly pushed above its reference level. A measured removal process increases until the concentration returns toward the reference. Which principle best matches the observation?
options: Matter is absent from the system
Negative feedback opposes the concentration change
The removal enzyme has a specific unmeasured structure
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: infer a principle from a data table
items.prompt: A table for a closed container shows total measured carbon of 12.0 mmol before a process and 12.0 mmol afterward, although the amounts in three chemical forms change. Which statement is supported?
options: Carbon is conserved while its distribution among forms changes
One form must be an unmeasured catalyst
Carbon concentration is controlled by negative feedback
Every chemical form remains individually constant
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: test response direction
items.prompt: Which pattern is the defining observable signature of negative feedback?
options: A response amplifies the initial deviation
A total remains equal before and after in a closed boundary
The response reduces the initial deviation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: a new regulated variable
items.prompt: Blood pressure falls below a reference value. Heart rate rises, and pressure moves back toward the reference. Which principle is directly represented?
options: Direct proportionality between pressure and time
Negative feedback opposing the pressure decrease
Conservation of pressure in a sealed system
Proof of one specific neural pathway
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: define the system boundary
items.prompt: Before using a conservation principle, which question is most important?
options: Does every component have the same numerical amount?
Is the most complex mechanism named?
Can the quantity cross the defined system boundary?
Does the graph use a preferred color scheme?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: conservation in a new display
items.prompt: A closed tank contains 8.0 mol of nitrogen atoms before a reaction and 8.0 mol afterward. The atoms appear in different molecules after the reaction. Which conclusion is warranted?
options: Nitrogen atoms are conserved while molecular forms change
Every molecule is conserved without rearrangement
Negative feedback restores each original molecule
An unmeasured catalyst supplies additional nitrogen
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: equation to words
items.prompt: Over a measured range, a sensor obeys S = 5C, where C is concentration in mmol/L and S is signal in mV. Which statement preserves the relation?
options: The signal is 5 mV for each 1 mmol/L of concentration
The signal is always 5 mV greater than the concentration
The concentration is 5 times the signal
The signal falls by 5 mV whenever concentration rises
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: equation to table
items.prompt: Which table row is consistent with E = 3n, where n is the number of events and E is energy in joules?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: text to equation
items.prompt: A sample volume V is two milliliters for every gram of mass m, and V is zero when m is zero. Which equation represents the statement?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: table to equation
items.prompt: A table lists (time in s, distance in m) as (0, 0), (2, 6), and (5, 15). Which equation preserves the relationship?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: table to verbal invariant
items.prompt: A table gives pressure P of 2, 6, and 10 kPa at input x values of 1, 3, and 5 units. Which statement best preserves the table?
options: Pressure remains constant as input changes
Pressure is 2 kPa per input unit
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: graph features to equation
items.prompt: A graph of product amount y versus reactant amount x is a straight line through (0, 0) and (4, 12). Which equation preserves the represented relation?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: locate the invariant in a table
items.prompt: When testing whether a table represents y = kx, which quantity should remain constant across nonzero rows?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: a new table
items.prompt: A table lists force F of 6, 15, and 24 N at displacement x of 2, 5, and 8 m. Which statement matches the data?
options: Force is 3 N per meter of displacement
Force is 8 N for every displacement
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: read slope and intercept separately
items.prompt: A straight-line graph passes through the origin and through (5, 20). Which pair of features must a matching equation preserve?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: text to graph-defining features
items.prompt: A response R begins at zero and increases by 4 units for every 1-unit increase in stimulus S. Which graph features represent the statement?
options: A line with slope 1 and intercept 4
A curve with decreasing slope and intercept 0
A straight line through the origin with slope 4
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: direct substitution
items.prompt: Use v = d/t. An object travels 24 m in 6 s. What is its average speed?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: track the target unit
items.prompt: Use F = ma. A 3 kg object has acceleration 4 m/s². What force is predicted?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: use a temperature change
items.prompt: Use Q = mcΔT. For m = 0.50 kg, c = 200 J/(kg·°C), and ΔT = 4.0 °C, what is Q?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: isolate time
items.prompt: Use v = d/t. A cart moves 45 m at an average speed of 5 m/s. How long does the trip take?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: select and substitute quantities
items.prompt: Use Q = mcΔT. A 0.30 kg sample with c = 600 J/(kg·°C) warms from 20 °C to 25 °C. What heat Q is absorbed?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: rearrange for mass
items.prompt: Use Q = mcΔT. A process transfers 1200 J and changes temperature by 4.0 °C. If c = 300 J/(kg·°C), what mass m is involved?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: map the temperature change
items.prompt: In Q = mcΔT, a sample warms from 18 °C to 23 °C. Which value belongs in the ΔT slot?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: apply heat relation again
items.prompt: Use Q = mcΔT. A 0.25 kg sample with c = 800 J/(kg·°C) warms from 12 °C to 15 °C. What is Q?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: isolate a factor in a product
items.prompt: If Q = mcΔT and m is the target, which rearrangement is equivalent?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: solve for a different factor
items.prompt: Use F = ma. A net force of 18 N produces an acceleration of 6 m/s². What mass m does the equation imply?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
